found_values.value: A 5 V linear regulator of its own for the bridges, which also supplies the bridge ADC's analogue supply (AVDD), fed from the board's selected input bus (6.0 to 20 V, R5 row). Not the IO board's 5 V rail. The bridge is excited from the ADC's own 5 V analogue supply and the excitation sense lines go to the ADC's reference input, so the measurement is ratiometric: noise and drift of the excitation cancel. The 5 V rail carries the display's 1.5 A continuous and 2 A peak over the link cable, and its tolerance at the IO board's own loads is open (V100). The ADC's AVDD must stay within 4.75 to 5.25 V (ADS1235 and ADS1261 recommended operating conditions). A regulator of its own holds that whatever the rail does. The excitation load moves to the input bus: at most 57 mA (V255 plus the ADC's AVDD)
found_values.source: ADS1235 datasheet SBAS824 (October 2018) section 9.2 Typical Application ('The excitation voltage provided to the bridge is the ADC power supply voltage (5 V) ... sense lines are connected to the reference inputs ... ratiometric operation that cancels noise and drift of the excitation voltage') and section 6.3 (AVDD 4.75 to 5.25 V), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ads1235.pdf; hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:338 and Research.md R5 row at checkout c25aa863372d; V100 (open, for research)

found_values.value: 350 Ω ± 5 Ω input (excitation) resistance per cell, the same for the thrust cell and both torque cells. The lowest is 345 Ω. With 3 cells on one 5.0 V excitation: 14.5 mA a cell, 43.5 mA for the three. No load cell is named in the tree. The value is read from a strain-gauge S-type load cell of the class that covers the thrust range of V258: HT Sensor TAS501, 5 to 5000 kg, input resistance 350 ± 5 Ω, output resistance 350 ± 3 Ω. Tedea-Huntleigh Model 620 gives the same 2.0 mV/V class. A cell with a higher bridge resistance draws less
found_values.source: HT Sensor TAS501 S-type load cell datasheet, Specifications table, https://cdn.sparkfun.com/assets/parts/1/2/2/3/8/TAS501.pdf; tree: no load cell named (grep of checkout c25aa863372d for load cell, thrust, torque, strain, bridge)

found_values.value: 2.0 mV/V for each of the 3 cells (TAS501: rated output 2.0 ± 0.005 mV/V; zero balance ±1.0 %FS). At the 5 V excitation of F3 that gives ±10.0 mV full scale per cell. The ADC must also take ±0.1 mV zero balance and 2 % over-range at 500 N on a 490.3 N cell: ±10.3 mV at most. Tedea-Huntleigh Model 620 (document 12059, 25-Jul-2012) also gives 2.0 mV/V
found_values.source: TAS501 datasheet, Specifications table, https://cdn.sparkfun.com/assets/parts/1/2/2/3/8/TAS501.pdf; Tedea-Huntleigh Model 620 datasheet, https://intertechnology.com/Tedea_Huntleigh/pdfs/620.pdf; F3 (5 V excitation)

found_values.value: Thrust cell: 490.3 N (50 kg). This is the TAS501 capacity step that covers the ±500 N of V258 within its 150 %FS safe overload (735 N). Torque cells: not read. Each torque cell's capacity is the torque range divided by the lever arm between the two cells. The lever arm is mechanical, round 3, and not stated in the tree
found_values.source: TAS501 datasheet (capacities 5 ... 50, 100 ... kg; safe overload 150 %FS), https://cdn.sparkfun.com/assets/parts/1/2/2/3/8/TAS501.pdf; V258

found_values.value: Thrust −500 N to +500 N; torque −30 N·m to +30 N·m. No figure is in the tree. These are the published ranges of the commercial thrust stand whose electrical class matches this bench: the Tyto Robotics Flight Stand 50, up to 180 V and 300 A. The bench's external path is above 150 A to 300 A and more (owner, 2026-09-25), and its pack is 67.2 V (F15). The same maker's Series 1585, 50 V and 55 A, measures thrust and torque on 3 load cells, as F3 does. It gives −5 to +5 kgf and −2 to +2 N·m and is too small for this bench's currents
found_values.source: Tyto Robotics Flight Stand 50 Datasheet, document FSFI50 V5.1 2026-08-10, Product Specifications (Thrust Range ±500 N, Torque Range ±30 Nm, Current up to 300 A, Voltage up to 180 V), https://cdn.tytorobotics.com/Documents/Datasheets/Flight-Stand-50-Datasheet.pdf; Series 1585 Datasheet AFU3XH V2.4 2024-08-01 Table 1 and page 7, https://cdn.rcbenchmark.com/landing_pages/Manuals/Series%201585%20Datasheet.pdf

found_values.value: Thrust cell: 0.05 N. Each torque cell: 1/10,000 of its capacity (Flight Stand 50: 0.003 N·m over ±30 N·m). In N this is not read, because the torque cells' capacity is not read (V257). Flight Stand 50 defines resolution as 3 times the standard deviation of the noise floor over 1 s at the full sample rate. On a 490.3 N, 2.0 mV/V cell at 5 V, 0.05 N is 1.02 µV at the ADC input. The bridge ADC's input-referred noise is therefore at most 0.34 µV RMS at the data rate it runs, at the output rate of V261
found_values.source: Flight Stand 50 Datasheet FSFI50 V5.1, Product Specifications (Thrust Resolution 0.05 N, Torque Resolution 0.003 Nm) and Technical definitions (Resolution), https://cdn.tytorobotics.com/Documents/Datasheets/Flight-Stand-50-Datasheet.pdf; V256, V257

found_values.value: 1.0 % of the cell's rated output, applied to every channel, over 0 to 50 °C (V264), after one calibration at one temperature. Flight Stand 50 Standard gives thrust ±5 N over ±500 N (1.0 %) and torque ±0.4 N·m over ±30 N·m (1.33 %). These are whole-system figures that include the cell and the calibration. The bridge ADC's and the excitation's gain and offset drift over 0 to 50 °C are held to the tighter 1.0 %. With ratiometric measurement (V254) the excitation's gain error and drift cancel
found_values.source: Flight Stand 50 Datasheet FSFI50 V5.1, Product Specifications (Thrust Accuracy ±5 N Standard; Torque Accuracy ±0.4 Nm Standard) and Technical definitions (Accuracy), https://cdn.tytorobotics.com/Documents/Datasheets/Flight-Stand-50-Datasheet.pdf

found_values.value: 100 samples per second per channel, on each of the 3 channels: the Flight Stand 50 Standard sampling rate. The Pro version samples at 1,000 Hz. The Series 1585 samples at up to 80 Hz. The coprocessor samples the bench numbers every 20 ms (50 Hz) (IOBoard.md:431, firmware/iomcu/src/main.c:1011-1016), and 100 SPS gives each 20 ms sample a fresh reading
found_values.source: Flight Stand 50 Datasheet FSFI50 V5.1 (Sampling rate 100 Hz Standard, 1,000 Hz Pro), https://cdn.tytorobotics.com/Documents/Datasheets/Flight-Stand-50-Datasheet.pdf; Series 1585 Datasheet page 2 (up to ~80 Hz); firmware/iomcu/src/main.c:1011-1016 at checkout c25aa863372d

found_values.value: One multiplexed converter may read the 3 channels in turn. The 3 readings of one set, the thrust cell and both torque cells, are taken within 10 ms, one output period at the 100 SPS of V261. Conversion at one instant is not required. The source is a derivation: V261 fixes one set every 10 ms. Neither the tree nor the Flight Stand 50 datasheet requires simultaneous conversion
found_values.source: derived from V261; Flight Stand 50 Datasheet FSFI50 V5.1 (one sampling rate for the thrust and torque set), https://cdn.tytorobotics.com/Documents/Datasheets/Flight-Stand-50-Datasheet.pdf

found_values.value: 4 wires: excitation + and −, signal + and −. TAS501: 4-core shielded PVC cable, 5 mm, 3 m. The board senses the reference at its own excitation terminals. A 6-wire cell, such as Tedea-Huntleigh Model 620 with its 2 sense wires, connects with its sense leads joined to its excitation leads at the connector. One reference input serves all 3 cells, because they share one excitation (V254)
found_values.source: TAS501 datasheet (Electrical connection: 4 core shielded PVC cable, excitation(+) red, excitation(−) black, signal(+) green, signal(−) white), https://cdn.sparkfun.com/assets/parts/1/2/2/3/8/TAS501.pdf; Tedea-Huntleigh Model 620 datasheet (6-wire cable, sense circuit), https://intertechnology.com/Tedea_Huntleigh/pdfs/620.pdf

found_values.value: 0 to 50 °C ambient. V7's answer sets one range for the whole IO board: '0 to 50 °C ambient, one range for the whole IO board (owner, 2026-09-28)'. For the stand itself, the TAS501 compensates −20 to +55 °C and operates −10 to +40 °C, and Flight Stand 50 operates 0 to 40 °C
found_values.source: Research.md, Raised by P1, V7 Answer column, at checkout c25aa863372d; TAS501 datasheet (operating −10 to +40 °C, compensated −20 to +55 °C), https://cdn.sparkfun.com/assets/parts/1/2/2/3/8/TAS501.pdf

found_values.value: 20 ms from a step in thrust or torque to a fully settled reading on that channel. This is the coprocessor's sampling period of the bench numbers, 20 ms (50 Hz), so a step is settled by the next bench sample after the one it lands in. For a converter reading 3 channels in turn: one full channel cycle, at most 10 ms by V262, plus one settled conversion of that channel
found_values.source: hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:431 and firmware/iomcu/src/main.c:1011-1016 ('if ((uint32_t)(now - last_sample) >= 20u) { sample(); ...') at checkout c25aa863372d; derivation with V261 and V262
